slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Yes: enter the US in 2027 Amazon-first, the only route inside the board's limits
The US is worth entering: K-beauty leads skincare growth, and Onsoo's pilot works
–	K-beauty sales nearly doubled to $3.6B in 2021–25, 39% of the category's growth
–	Amazon carries 41% of K-beauty sales; Onsoo's pilot units nearly doubled in six months
Retail-led breaks the cash cap, payback and margin floor, even on its own inputs
–	Retail-led cash falls to −$20.8M by 2030, past the $18M cap; Amazon-led pays back in 2030
–	Retail earns back 29% of its $31.6M spend; group margin falls to 4.5% in 2027
Its inputs are also too optimistic: at Onsoo's awareness, stores would delist it
–	The plan's 4.5 units per door a week fits brands above 20% awareness; Onsoo has 4%
–	At 2.6 units a door and no halo, retail-led would lose about $26.4M by 2030
Amazon-led fits every limit, but pays back only if ad cost stays at or below 28.6%
–	At the 32% benchmark ACoS, cash ends 2030 at −$2.3M; even at 38%, the gap is 35% of the cap
We recommend Amazon-led entry in 2027, a restated ambition and gated retail
–	Amazon-led reaches $26.4M in 2030: 66% of the ambition, nearly four times Japan's
–	Five guardrails govern the launch; the CEO's retail gate moves from 15% to 20% awareness

slides.title: Neither the halo nor peer history supports retail-first, and Amazon-first worked for one entrant in three

paragraphs.text: 1 Opportunity    2 Economics    3 Retail inputs    4 Amazon risk    5 Plan
Neither the halo nor peer history supports retail-first, and Amazon-first worked for one entrant in three
The 1.3 times halo rests on a correlation, not a cause
Saebom went Amazon-first and added stores once sales were proven
Mooncrest went retail-first and lost more than our whole cash cap
Amazon-first is no guarantee: two of three such entrants stayed small
▪	Across 30 K-beauty brands, doors and Amazon sales correlate at 0.71
▪	Brands that sell well on Amazon win more doors, so the arrow can run either way
▪	Only 17% of K-beauty buyers found their last new brand in a store, against 38% on TikTok
▪	Entered the US on Amazon in 2022
▪	Reached about $30M of US revenue by 2025
▪	Added 300 specialty doors in 2025, three years after entry
▪	Launched in 450 doors in 2023
▪	Removed from shelves in 2025, after the retailer's review
▪	Estimated cumulative US loss above the board's $18M cap
▪	Gaon Lab entered on Amazon in 2022
▪	Yeoreum entered on Amazon in 2023
▪	Both stayed below that US revenue in 2025, hence the guardrails in section 5

Payback is at risk; the cash cap is not
▪	Benchmark, 32%: the median for brands scaling from $5M to $20M on Amazon, the band Onsoo's plan crosses
▪	Duty 25%: the tariff decision due in mid-2027 costs about $1.1M of cumulative cash by 2030

The line sits just above the pilot and well below the benchmark
▪	Volumes as planned: 2,810,000 Amazon units over 2027–30 from seven SKUs
